# Dhammacetiya Sutta (MN 89 (PTS MN ii 118))

**ID:** MN 89 (PTS MN ii 118)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Dhammacetiya Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Shrines to the Teaching
**PTS:** MN ii 118

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammacetiya Sutta* ("Shrines to the Teaching" or "Monuments to the Dhamma") is the 89th discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya*, situated within the *Majjhimapaṇṇāsaka* [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Payuto; SuttaCentral]. Set in the Sakyan town of Medaḷumpa while King Pasenadi of Kosala was staying nearby at Nagaraka, the sutta depicts a poignant visit by Pasenadi to the Buddha near the end of the king's life [Burlingame 1921; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; SuttaCentral]. Pasenadi expresses profound veneration, listing ten reasons why the Buddha and his monastic community are superior to all other teachers and ascetics [Allon 2001; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Rogell 2003]. Among these reasons, the king observes that while kings, nobles, and householders constantly quarrel, the Buddha's monks dwell in peace, harmony, and concord, dedicated to the holy life in quiet lodgings suitable for seclusion [Hazra 1994; Karashima 2012; Humphreys 1956]. Pasenadi also highlights their shared Kosalan identity and age [Wynne 2007; SuttaCentral]. According to the commentary and related narrative traditions, this discourse represents the final meeting between the king and the Buddha, as Pasenadi's general Dīghakārāyana defected with the royal insignia during the visit to crown Viḍūḍabha, leaving the deposed monarch to die shortly thereafter [Burlingame 1921; Rogell 2003].

In the Gāndhārī Senior manuscripts collection, texts identified as parallels to the *Dhammacetiya Sutta* similarly articulate the theme of the Buddha's and his Sangha's pre-eminence [Allon 2001]. SuttaCentral identifies full parallels in the Pāli *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10.30), the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 213) and *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 38.10), the Tibetan Kangyur (*Vinayakṣudrakavastu*, D 6), and the *Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya* (T 1451.8) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus's automated analysis confirms extensive alignments with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26, fascicle 59) and the Tibetan *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* (D 6), as well as significant Pāli-internal text reuse with AN 10.30, the *Cūḷahatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 27), the *Vinaya Piṭaka* (*Khandhaka* texts Kd 1, Kd 6, and Kd 8), and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [DharmaNexus].
